messages:
raj: Heads up — started seeing sporadic TLS failures for some EU inference routes after the cert rotation. Some clients get 503, others see TLS alert handshake_failure.

emily: Yep, saw a spike in failed requests around 04:12 UTC in Datadog for eu-region. Traces show TLS handshake errors before request hits backend.

matt: I did a quick curl from an EU bastion to reproduce: 
```
curl -v https://gateway.eu.redwood.ai/health -H 'Host: model.redwood.ai'
```
Result: TLS handshake then certificate presented is CN=collector.internal (internal CA) -> client rejects.

sara: That smells like SNI vs Host header mismatch. ALB selects cert based on SNI. Our ingress/controller then routes by Host header. If client SNI != Host header we can end up with a cert that doesn't chain publicly (and breaks mTLS).

raj: Confirmed: affected clients include our internal collectors that set SNI=collector.internal but Host=model.redwood.ai. Public clients send matching SNI and Host and are fine.

deploy-bot: deploy: cert-rotation-eu completed at 2026-03-17T04:10:12Z (job id: rot-eu-2026-03-17).

matt: Reproducer using openssl: 
```
openssl s_client -connect gateway.eu.redwood.ai:443 -servername collector.internal -showcerts
```
Server certificate CN=collector.internal (signed by internal CA) — so ALB chose internal cert based on SNI.

emily: Interesting: our logs show the bulk of failures are TLS1.3 + ALPN h2. Older TLS1.2 clients largely unaffected.

sara: Temporary mitigation options: 1) force ALB to present the public cert for certain hostnames (listener rule), 2) change clients to send SNI matching Host, or 3) proxy rewrite SNI at edge (envoy) before TLS termination (hard).

raj: Changing client SNI is preferable long-term but risky for collectors. We need a quick canary for customer-facing traffic.

matt: I can push a listener rule to the eu canary ALB to prefer public cert for traffic to /v1/models/* and host model.redwood.ai. It'll be a non-disruptive rule (higher priority), we can roll back quickly.

emily: I'll try an Envoy SNI-rewrite on a small canary cluster to see if rewriting SNI to Host header before the ALB sees it fixes the path. If it works we can use that as a stopgap.

sara: Action items: 
- emily: deploy envoy SNI-rewrite canary and report success/failure by 05:00 UTC (timeline: 30m).
- matt: prepare ALB listener rule with rollback playbook (I'll stage the change in a maintenance window).
- raj: coordinate with collectors team about SNI config and start risk assessment for client change.

raj: I'll open a runbook and notify oncall channels. Reconnect at 05:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

emily: noted, I'll post results to this thread once the canary is up.

sara: Thanks — also add a Datadog dashboard tile for cert-presented-CN by source IP so we can quickly identify which clients get internal certs.

matt: Will do.

raj: Thanks team. Keeping this thread for updates.
